title: Open Comet and ask about the page you see
summary: Comet is Perplexity’s web browser. Its assistant can help you read an open page.
where: On Windows or Mac, visit perplexity.ai/comet for the official download. On an iPad, use the iOS App Store link from that page. Comet is also available on Android.

actions.title: Open the browser
actions.do: Install Comet and open it. You can practice without importing bookmarks or making it the default browser.
actions.see: You reach a browser window with an address field.
actions.stuck: A tab at perplexity.ai in Safari is Perplexity Search. This exercise uses the separate Comet app.

actions.title: Visit one public page
actions.do: Enter example.com in the address field. Read its heading.
actions.see: The heading is “Example Domain.”
actions.stuck: If a search results page opens, enter https://example.com as a complete address.

actions.title: Ask about that page
actions.do: Open the Assistant in Comet. Ask “What is the heading of my current page? Give the address you used.”
actions.see: Its answer should identify Example Domain at example.com.
actions.stuck: On desktop look for the assistant beside the page. On mobile open its assistant control. Share the current tab if prompted.

actions.title: Check the context
actions.do: Open example.org in a new tab and ask the same question.
actions.see: The heading is similar but the address should now end in .org.
actions.stuck: If it still quotes .com, explicitly select the second tab or start the assistant from that tab.

roles: Read a public Exchange help page.
Check which admin guide a summary cites.

title: Ask Perplexity Search and inspect its source
summary: Perplexity Search writes answers with links to its sources. Learn to check the sentence behind one answer.
where: Open perplexity.ai in a browser. Standard Search is enough. You can use it in Safari or an existing desktop browser.

actions.title: Find the question field
actions.do: Open the Perplexity homepage and start a fresh question. Choose a normal search if the screen offers several tools.
actions.see: A box accepts words and a send control runs the search.
actions.stuck: Return to the home or new search screen if you see an old conversation.

actions.title: Ask a narrow question
actions.do: Send “Which agency launched Apollo 11? Give the launch date and link to NASA’s Apollo 11 mission page.”
actions.see: Look for NASA and July 16, 1969 with an attached source.
actions.stuck: If it answers only with a moon landing date, ask specifically for the launch date.

actions.title: Open the citation
actions.do: Select the source next to the claim. Check the publisher and find the date on the mission page.
actions.see: A NASA page should support July 16 as the launch date.
actions.stuck: If the link goes to a fan page or a generic homepage, ask for the mission page and open the replacement citation.

actions.title: Test a second fact
actions.do: Ask “Which date was the Moon landing? Keep it separate from launch.”
actions.see: The landing date is July 20, 1969.
actions.stuck: Look at the event label as well as the date. Different events in one mission have different dates.

roles: Check a public support statement at its source.
Find the original rollout notice behind a summary.
Verify which library release a claim describes.

title: Give Grok Bot a first file-making job
summary: Grok Bot is an agent that can work on files on its cloud computer. Give it a task with an answer you can open.
where: On a computer visit x.ai/bot and use its official download. The getting-started guide covers macOS, Windows and Linux and links its mobile options. Use an eligible account or seat shown at sign-in.

actions.title: Sign in to the Bot app
actions.do: Open the installed app, choose Sign in and finish the account step in the browser. Return to Grok Bot.
actions.see: The Bot workspace opens when your account has access.
actions.stuck: If you see an access screen, read its account-linking options. A working ordinary Grok chat does not establish Bot access.

actions.title: Create a practice Bot
actions.do: Choose New Bot or the plus at the top of the sidebar. Give the Bot the name List Maker.
actions.see: Your new Bot has a place to send messages.
actions.stuck: On a team, select Create a Bot from the plus menu if offered.

actions.title: Give it a local file job
actions.do: Send “Create a small CSV file called fruit.csv with columns Name,Count and two rows: Pear,2 and Plum,3. Return the file here.”
actions.see: Look for a CSV attachment in its reply.
actions.stuck: If it only prints a table, ask for a downloadable CSV file in the conversation. It needs no account connection for these values.

actions.title: Read the result
actions.do: Open the returned file. Check the header, rows and total.
actions.see: There are two fruit records and five pieces of fruit.
actions.stuck: If the preview is unclear, download the file and open it in a text editor or spreadsheet.

roles: Rehearse making a report from synthetic data.
Make a CSV fixture for an importer.
sources: xAI · sign in and make a Bot

title: Open Mistral Vibe and make a short checklist
summary: Vibe is Mistral’s assistant for work and code. Try the work view with a task that needs no connected apps.
where: Open chat.mistral.ai in a browser and sign in. If an older guide calls it Le Chat, Mistral now uses Vibe.

actions.title: Find the work area
actions.do: Choose Work from the sidebar mode selector if you see modes. On accounts with a combined Chat and Work view, use the main writing box.
actions.see: You can enter a work request.
actions.stuck: If you are in Code and it asks for a repository, switch to Work for this checklist.

actions.title: Provide a tiny job
actions.do: Send “From these facts make a two-item packing checklist: carry the cabin key and charge the phone.”
actions.see: The answer contains two actions.
actions.stuck: If it adds travel tips, ask it to use only the two actions you provided.

actions.title: Ask for a clearer format
actions.do: Send “Put one unchecked box before each item and keep each line to five words.”
actions.see: Each action has its own short checklist line.
actions.stuck: If the boxes are not clickable, text symbols like ☐ are enough for this exercise.

actions.title: Check a small revision
actions.do: Send “Replace phone with tablet and leave the first item alone.”
actions.see: You should see a cabin key item and a tablet item.
actions.stuck: If the entire checklist changes, quote the first line you want kept.

roles: Draft a synthetic two-step mail checklist.
Prepare short instructions for a training group.
Test how text fits on a checklist screen.
sources: Mistral · Le Chat is now Vibe

title: Turn one photo into a short clip in Firefly
summary: Adobe Firefly can make a video using a picture as its first frame. Inspect the result for unwanted changes.
where: Open firefly.adobe.com on a computer and sign in. Use a simple photo you took, such as a mug on a table. Video access and the credits charged depend on the model and plan.

actions.title: Open the video tool
actions.do: Find Video, then Generate video. Open the controls for a starting frame.
actions.see: You should see a prompt field and an option for a first image.
actions.stuck: If you only see image generation, return to the video area. A photo preview alone does not make a clip.

actions.title: Supply the starting picture
actions.do: Under Frame or Frames, add your photo as the first frame. Keep the last frame empty for this exercise.
actions.see: The photo appears as the starting picture.
actions.stuck: If it looks cut off, inspect the shape of the video frame and choose a closer match.

actions.title: Describe one motion
actions.do: Enter “Slowly move the camera closer to the mug. Keep the mug still and the room unchanged.” Check the displayed generation cost before selecting Generate.
actions.see: With video access and sufficient credits, a playable clip appears.
actions.stuck: If generation is unavailable, keep the source and prompt as a storyboard. A storyboard is a plan, not a rendered video.

actions.title: Play and inspect
actions.do: Play the result twice. Compare the opening to the photo, then watch the handle and background near the end.
actions.see: The intended motion is a camera move; extra handles or a shifting object are visible errors.
actions.stuck: If the motion is too busy, reduce the description to one slow camera move and retry only if you intend to use more credits.

roles: Mock up a visual intro for a how-to.
Create a short preview clip for an app screen.

title: Change just one part of a picture
summary: Put a tiny orange sailboat next to a mug. First show Firefly exactly where the new object belongs.
where: Use Firefly on a computer with your Adobe account. A plain photo you took of a mug on a table works well. Leave an empty patch of table beside it.
If you are using the mobile app, choose Generative fill, then upload the photo. The controls shown in the picture come from Adobe’s demonstration.

actions.title: Open the picture
actions.do: In Firefly choose Image, then Edit image. Upload your photo and choose Fill in the editing tools. On a phone use the brush tool inside Generative fill.
actions.see: The full photo appears with a brush control. You can see the mug and the empty tabletop.
actions.stuck: If you see a blank text-to-image box, switch to Edit and choose your existing picture.

actions.title: Paint the space
actions.do: Brush a patch on the table beside the mug. Imagine where the little boat’s base would sit. Stop before your brush touches the mug.
actions.see: A colored overlay shows the area you have selected. This colored paint is a guide for the tool.
actions.stuck: If you paint over the mug, choose Select less or the subtract control and brush that part of the selection away.

actions.title: Describe one object
actions.do: Type “a small orange toy sailboat standing on the table.” Select Fill or Generate. Wait for the result before deciding whether to use it.
actions.see: The boat should sit inside the marked area. Look at both its size and its contact with the table.
actions.stuck: If the boat floats above the table, change the selected area to include the surface below the boat and try again.

actions.title: Compare the whole photo
actions.do: Look at the mug’s handle, its shadow and the edge of the table. Pick a variation only after checking all three. Save a new copy.
actions.see: You have an original and an edited picture. You can point out the one change you intended.
actions.stuck: If the mug has changed shape, return to the original and use a narrower selection. Preserve the original for comparison.

roles: Use a made-up picture when illustrating a help note.
Practice image editing on a training slide you own.
Add a prop to a book-cover prototype before choosing final artwork.
sources: Adobe · Generative Fill on the web
